#### Universality: linear everywhere; nonlinearity needs a smooth basis {#sec-singonly-universality}

Two checks complete the picture (checked-in key
`iteration_13_singonly_universality`).

**Screened Laplace: singular-only is best-in-class there too** (three
seeds, 2,000 steps, the exact protocol of @sec-screened):

| screened arm (3-seed means) | ID | low-$\tilde\kappa$ | high-$\tilde\kappa$ | unseen modes | PDE residual |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 8 MLP members | 0.0144 | 0.0443 | 0.1835 | 0.1842 | 0.562 |
| singular + poly | 0.0120 | 0.0414 | 0.1847 | 0.0192 | 0.568 |
| **singular only** | **0.0099** | **0.0345** | **0.1657** | 0.0206 | — |

: Screened Laplace, singular-only against the iteration-9 arms. The
singular-only archived runs predate fidelity-first reporting, hence the
em-dash (@sec-fidelity-columns). {#tbl-screened-singonly}

The $\tilde\kappa$-conditioning **survives a one-member dictionary**: the
operator encoder carries the parameter dependence into the coefficients
of a single exact kernel.

**Nonlinear Liouville: catastrophic failure.** The same pruning in
`zero_preserving_nonlinear` field mode (1,500 steps, the exact protocol
of @sec-liouville) destroys the model: ID 0.9583 / 36.5348 / 2.30 across
seeds 17/18/19 — seed 18 outright diverged — against $\sim$0.46–0.48 for
both polynomial-bearing nonlinear arms and 0.769 for the linear wall
itself. In nonlinear field mode the polynomial members are
**load-bearing** for the drive-nonlinear correction.

The closing rule of the dictionary program (the artifact's
`refined_rule`, restated in @sec-decoder-role):

> **The dictionary carries the singularity; conditioning carries the
> smoothness; nonlinearity needs a smooth basis.** In drive-linear
> operation the dictionary is the exact singular member(s) alone —
> best-in-class on 2D Laplace, screened Laplace, and 3D Laplace alike.
> In nonlinear field mode the polynomial members are load-bearing. MLP
> members are prunable everywhere.

One question stays open: is the nonlinear failure representational or an
optimization instability? A cosine-decay rerun of nonlinear singular-only
would decide it; under the redirect that discriminator is *parked* with
the protocol-hygiene items (@sec-future).

*History: @sec-nb-iter12.*

### The single-layer member and hard geometry {#sec-single-layer}

**Two exact singular members are the default dictionary for hard
geometry; the honest cost is extrapolation on easy geometry.** The
second member is the **single-layer potential** alongside the double
layer (2D Hess–Smith segment closed form; 3D per-edge
$\operatorname{asinh}$ plus solid-angle form; quadrature validated to
$\sim 10^{-14}$; +276 parameters, the `singpair` arm at 104,537 —
exactly two exact singular members). It entered as a targeted
fix for the shell tier and failed its pre-registered prediction there
(the arc is @sec-nb-iter16); what survived contact with the data is a
sharper rule, established on the encoder-stress suites — the
multiply connected multi-body family and the deep-cavity family with
its convex control, defined in @sec-encoder-stress
(`encoder_stress_head_to_head`; pair-kernel rows are the 1,500-step
control references):

| multi-body (3-seed means) | ID | narrow gap | single body | unseen charges | PDE residual | max-principle viol. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| MeshTransformer, singular-only | 0.115 | 0.246 | 0.153 | 0.153 | — | — |
| **MeshTransformer, sing+single-layer** | **0.065** | **0.160** | **0.102** | **0.087** | — | — |
| free-form pair kernel (control) | 0.097 | 0.242 | 0.161 | 0.160 | — | — |

: Multi-body head-to-head, three seeds. The two fidelity columns (this
suite is harmonic Dirichlet, so both the strong-form residual and the
sampled maximum-principle violation are licensed) are em-dashed: the
archived runs predate fidelity-first reporting (@sec-fidelity-columns).
{#tbl-multibody}

| deep cavity | ID (2-seed mean) | deep slot (3-seed mean) | convex control (2-seed mean) | PDE residual |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| MeshTransformer, singular-only | 0.098 | 0.393 | 0.083 | — |
| **MeshTransformer, sing+single-layer** | **0.067** | **0.240** | 0.071 | — |
| free-form pair kernel (control) | 0.115 | 0.265 | 0.084 | — |

: Deep-cavity head-to-head (the deep-slot column is closed at three
seeds, `deep_cavity_final_n3`; the other columns are two-seed means).
PDE residual em-dashed: archived runs predate fidelity-first reporting
(@sec-fidelity-columns). {#tbl-deepcavity}

What this establishes:

- **On multiply connected data the single-layer member is decisively
  load-bearing.** `singpair` sweeps all 12 split-seed comparisons against
  singular-only and beats the pair-kernel control everywhere; *without*
  it, the `MeshTransformer` loses to the pair kernel in-distribution
  (0.115 vs 0.097) — the double layer's flux deficiency binds exactly
  where the data carries winding content.
- **The gate is not purely topological.** Deep cavity is simply connected
  and the member helps there too (deep-slot 0.240 vs 0.393, ID 0.067 vs
  0.098). The rule: **two exact singular members are the default
  dictionary for hard geometry; the honest cost is extrapolation on easy
  geometry** (the 2D star-bank freq-OOD regresses 0.075 $\to$ 0.17–0.27
  with the member present). The mechanism is conditioned-coefficient
  freedom: in classical BIE the single-layer density is determined by the
  boundary system, while here it is freely fit, so on easy domains SGD
  spends the member's smooth far field on interpolation.
- **On the hardest OOD tier the architecture is competitive**: singpair's
  deep-slot 0.240 matches-or-beats the 19k-parameter pair-kernel
  control's 0.265, and the singular-only arm's loss there (0.393) is the
  hard-geometry rule again, not a separate defect.

*History: @sec-nb-iter16 — the failed shell prediction, the Betti-gate
hypothesis that did not survive, and a two-seed failure flag that the
third seed downgraded.*

### Are the vector channels load-bearing? {#sec-scalar-only}

The vector channels stay: not load-bearing on easy 2D geometry,
genuinely load-bearing off it — and the gap is oriented transport, not
width. They are a substantial share of the stack's complexity
(@sec-typed-channels), so the question got the
sharpest of the component-level questions (@sec-future).
**Scalar-only mode** ablates oriented state *transport* between cells:
the latent state carries no vector channels, so no orientation
information propagates through the attention layers. Normals do not
vanish from the model — they still enter through the decoder's pair
invariants and through scalar Gram invariants at the lift. The default
vector-ful path is bitwise-preserved (scalar-only is opt-in), and the
parameter count drops $\approx$60%: singular-only 104,261 $\to$ 41,941.
Checked-in key `iteration_14_scalar_only_2d` (with
`wide_scalar_capacity_control`).

**2D Laplace: not load-bearing.** At the reference protocol (3,000
steps, seeds 17/29/43):

| arm (3-seed means) | params | ID | unseen geometry | stronger deformation | freq-OOD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|

inter-cell state transport is genuine physics capacity off plain 2D
geometry — the vector channels stay.** Two side observations: modes-OOD
and the shell tier are indifferent to the ablation (the shell error is

@sec-single-layer), and the MLP-member freq-OOD destruction persists in

*History: @sec-nb-iter14.*

### Heads versus rank at fixed score capacity {#sec-heads-vs-rank}

**Splitting attention into heads at fixed total score capacity is
bookkeeping — and blocking the value maps into head groups is a
restriction that buys nothing measured.** The setup (checked-in key
`iteration_31_heads_vs_rank`; pre-registered design in
`studies/heads_rank_study.py`): per attention head the effective score
matrix has rank at most $R_0 + DR_1$ (module README §7), so one layer's
pair-coefficient class is determined by the **total** score capacity
$H(R_0 + DR_1)$ — an early design-review note proved heads and separable
rank enter the score identically, suggesting the head count is pure
capacity bookkeeping. But heads remain distinct *after* the scores: the
value spaces are head-blocked (`dim // heads` per head) and the typed
output maps contract head-by-head. Three singpair arms hold the total at
exactly $80$ ($D = 2$; the ranks divide evenly, no rounding), on the 2D
Laplace reference bank at 3,000 steps, seeds 17/29/43, the iteration-26
finalist evaluation bank — the reference row *is* @tbl-stream-laplace's
two-stream row, reproduced to all four archived decimals. Pre-registered
rule: per probe arm and split, a 3-seed mean within twice the larger
seed sd of the reference is a match; all cells matching means heads are
bookkeeping, any decisive miss localizes the effect in the per-head
value/output structure — the only unmatched machinery.

| arm (3-seed mean ± sd) | $H$ | $R_0/R_1$ | params | ID | unseen geometry | stronger deformation | freq-OOD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| reference | 4 | 12/4 | 104,537 | 0.0485 ± 0.0025 | 0.0686 ± 0.0070 | 0.0862 ± 0.0148 | 0.2111 ± 0.0523 |
| one head | 1 | 48/16 | 104,123 | **0.0413 ± 0.0021** | 0.0624 ± 0.0018 | 0.0825 ± 0.0058 | 0.1831 ± 0.0158 |
| eight heads | 8 | 6/2 | 104,897 | 0.0461 ± 0.0014 | 0.0669 ± 0.0041 | 0.0812 ± 0.0147 | 0.2077 ± 0.0471 |

: Heads traded against separable ranks at fixed total score capacity
$H(R_0 + 2R_1) = 80$, singpair dictionary, matched parameters within
0.4%. Relative $L^2$ per split; bold marks the one cell outside the
pre-registered tolerance. {#tbl-heads-vs-rank}

What this establishes:

- **Eight heads are bookkeeping.** At halved ranks the 8-head arm
  matches the reference within tolerance on every split — largest
  $|\Delta|$ 0.0050 on stronger deformation against a 0.0296 tolerance;
  on ID, $\Delta$ $-0.0024$ against 0.0050 — exactly what the one-layer
  algebra predicts.
- **One head is not — it is better.** The single full-width head at
  quadrupled ranks wins ID decisively (0.0413 vs 0.0485, $\Delta$
  $-0.0072$ against a $\pm 0.0050$ tolerance, i.e. 2.9$\times$ the
  larger seed sd — a 15% error reduction), is directionally better on
  all four splits, is the most seed-stable arm (geometry sd 0.0018 vs
  0.0070; freq-OOD sd 0.0158 vs 0.0523), and has the *fewest*
  parameters (104,123, $-0.40$%).
- **Localization, by construction.** The score-coefficient class was
  matched exactly, so the one-head gain prices the head-blocking of the
  value/output maps: with $H = 1$ the drive values ride full-width
  (48 scalar / 12 vector) maps instead of four aligned blocks. The
  aligned-moment-group restriction buys nothing measured here.
- **Scope, stated plainly:** one PDE, one capacity point, three seeds;
  the win is decisive under the pre-registered rule but modest in
  magnitude. The parsimony question — default to one head? — moves to
  the roadmap (@sec-future) rather than flipping the reference config
  on a single-benchmark result. (Since resolved:
  @sec-one-head-cross-suite.)

*History: @sec-nb-iter31.*

### One head across suites: the confirmation, and what it did not confirm {#sec-one-head-cross-suite}

The cross-suite follow-up the previous section demanded (checked-in key
`iteration_32_one_head_cross_suite`; pre-registered design and flip rule
in `studies/one_head_cross_suite.py`). One capacity-preserving one-head
variant per suite — heads $4 \to 1$, ranks $12/4 \to 48/16$, an identity
that holds the total score capacity $H(R_0 + DR_1)$ fixed in *every*
spatial dimension — trained at three seeds against the **archived**
4-head comparators, protocols matched run-for-run and nothing re-trained:
screened Laplace (`singonly_h1`, 2,000 steps, vs
`iteration_13_singonly_universality`), potential-flow velocity
(`singpair_pseudo_h1`, pseudo sector `drive_pseudo_dim=8` untouched,
3,000 steps, vs the five archived seeds of
`iteration_23_pseudoscalar_extension`), and 3D Laplace (`singpair_h1`,
3,000 steps, vs `iteration_16_single_layer_member`). Pre-registered
rule, declared for a *default change*: per split, one head
matches-or-beats iff its 3-seed mean exceeds the archived mean by no
more than twice the larger seed sd; the reference configuration flips to
one head iff every split of at least two suites matches-or-beats and no
split anywhere is a decisive loss; any decisive loss and heads stay at
four, with iteration 31 recorded as Laplace-specific.

What this establishes:

- **The falsifier did not fire.** Thirteen of thirteen cells
  match-or-beat; all three suites pass on every split. Under the
  pre-registered rule the reference configuration **flips to one
  full-width head** (heads 1, ranks 48/16) — the next parsimony rung
  after the one-layer encoder and the two-member dictionary: fewer
  heads, fewer parameters on every suite, one less architectural degree
  of freedom, and nowhere measurably worse.
- **What the confirmation did *not* confirm, stated plainly:** the
  iteration-31 *win* did not travel. The 15% Laplace ID gain reappears
  nowhere; one head is directionally worse on 11 of 13 cells (both
  exceptions are mode-OOD splits). The cross-suite evidence is
  **non-inferiority, not superiority** — the flip is carried by
  parsimony, with the Laplace ID win recorded as Laplace-specific.
- **A bias in the rule, named:** the tolerance keys to the larger of
  the two arms' seed sds, so the noisier arm buys itself slack — the
  closest cell (screened ID, $+0.0107$ against $0.0135$) is within
  tolerance partly because the one-head arm's own spread is 2.3$\times$
  the archived one. Three seeds bound the claim: these are
  within-tolerance ties, not proof of equivalence.
- **The pseudo sector composes.** The one-head trade leaves
  `drive_pseudo_dim=8` untouched (its per-head split widens $2 \to 8$
  exactly as the scalar channels do), and circulation-OOD stays at the
  typed-circulation level — the @sec-pseudo-extension fix survives the
  head change.
- **Standing falsifier:** the flip reverts if any future suite shows a
  decisive one-head loss. The frozen benchmark capacity configs and
  every archived arm stay bitwise as recorded; the flip lands in the
  documented reference configuration (@sec-reference-config, 81,961
  $\to$ 81,547 parameters).

*History: @sec-nb-iter32.*

### Encoder depth {#sec-encoder-depth}

How much boundary self-attention does the physics need? On the
**all-Dirichlet** stress family the answer is *approximately none*: enc0
— zero boundary self-attention layers, 59,385 parameters — matches the
full two-layer `singpair` on the multi-body family of
@sec-encoder-stress at two seeds (seed 17: ID 0.073
vs 0.070; seed 18: 0.067 against the singpair three-seed mean of 0.065;
checked-in key `iteration_18_encoder_depth`). This is expected, not anomalous: the
Dirichlet double-layer density solves a second-kind Fredholm system
dominated by the local $\tfrac12 I$ term (@sec-pde-theory), so the
boundary-to-boundary solve is nearly local even though the
boundary-to-interior map is not. The genuine attention-necessity test is
therefore mixed and Neumann boundary conditions — the next section —
where the answer changes.

*History: @sec-nb-iter18.*

### The mixed-BC discriminator: where attention earns its keep {#sec-mixed-bc}

**Attention earns its keep exactly where the boundary solve is
genuinely nonlocal — and one encoder layer suffices even there.** The
pre-registered hypothesis behind that verdict: mixed-BC Cauchy solves
are nonlocal — unknown Dirichlet data on one boundary must be inferred
from Neumann data on another — where the all-Dirichlet solve is
$\tfrac12 I$-dominated and nearly local; therefore encoder depth should
matter on mixed problems where it did not on Dirichlet
(@sec-encoder-depth). One honest setup constraint: the 3D generator
assigns BC types *per boundary*, so the shell tier — inner boundary
carrying the Dirichlet trace, outer boundary carrying the Neumann flux —
is the only genuinely mixed tier available. Arms
(`mixed_bc_study.py`): `mt_singpair_mixed` at operator depths 2/1/0
(104,713 / 82,137 / 59,561 parameters), 3,000 steps, seeds 17/18/19,
splits `shell_mixed` and `shell_mixed_fine` (resolution OOD); checked-in
key `iteration_19_mixed_bc_discriminator`.

| operator depth | params | seed 17 | seed 18 | seed 19 | mean | fine (mean) | PDE residual |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| enc2 | 104,713 | 0.0479 | 0.0374 | 0.0614 | 0.049 | 0.070 | — |
| enc1 | 82,137 | 0.0534 | 0.0423 | 0.0576 | 0.051 | 0.060 | — |
| enc0 | 59,561 | 0.0612 | 0.1120 | 0.0650 | 0.079 | 0.102 | — |

: The mixed-BC depth sweep on the shell tier (`shell_mixed` relative
$L^2$ per seed; last column is the `shell_mixed_fine` resolution-OOD
mean). PDE residual em-dashed: archived runs predate fidelity-first
reporting; no maximum principle is licensed here — the outer boundary
carries flux data, so the known Dirichlet trace bounds nothing
(@sec-fidelity-columns). {#tbl-mixed-bc}

What this establishes — the hypothesis, confirmed in direction with a
parsimony twist. enc0 degrades on mixed BCs (mean 0.079 against 0.049),
and the honest characterization of *how* is **unreliability, not uniform
degradation**: seed 18 is catastrophic (0.112, and 0.182 on the fine
split) while the other seeds are merely worse. Meanwhile **enc1 matches
enc2** (0.051 vs 0.049). Attention earns its keep exactly where the
Fredholm structure is nonlocal, and **one encoder layer suffices** — the
second layer is prunable even here. A physics note worth one sentence:
`shell_mixed` at 0.049 is 7$\times$ easier than the all-Dirichlet shell
tier (0.37, @sec-dictionary-3d) — handing the model the outer flux
explicitly removes the winding-inference difficulty.

Caveats, from the archive: a single mixed geometry tier (the
per-boundary BC assignment permits no other); and `drive_layers` was
held at 1 in every arm — the genuinely nonlocal *data* coupling lives in
the drive blocks, so a drive-depth sweep is the sharper follow-up,
parked unless a sharper claim is needed (@sec-future).

*History: @sec-nb-iter19.*

### The intrinsic gauge: scale equivariance made unconditional {#sec-intrinsic-gauge}

Scale equivariance is now **unconditional**: the reference length is
derived from the geometry itself, so there is no convention left for a
caller to get wrong. The evidence trail (checked-in key
`iteration_24_intrinsic_gauge`; the change itself is documented in
@sec-forward-pass, per that chapter's contract). The reference length —
until now the one externally-trusted input, a caller-supplied
`reference_length` key — is derived **intrinsically by default**: the
measure-weighted RMS radius of the boundary about its center (the radius
of gyration), computed in fp64 and differentiable. The explicit key
remains as a bitwise-preserved override for canonically-dimensioned
applications. Three pre-registered checks, all confirmed:

| arm (3-seed means, reference protocol) | ID | freq-OOD | sim. covariance |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| intrinsic gauge (new default) | 0.0372 | 0.0750 | 2.9–3.1$\times$10$^{-7}$ |
| explicit key (override) | 0.0375 | 0.0748 | — |

: Gauge neutrality on the frozen reference bank. {#tbl-intrinsic-gauge}

- **Gauge neutrality**: the intrinsic gauge is accuracy-neutral at three
  seeds (ID 0.0372 vs 0.0375; freq and geometry splits likewise) — the
  model never needed the caller's number, only *a* consistent gauge.
- **Convention drift, demonstrated**: corrupt the supplied
  `reference_length` by 3$\times$ at evaluation time and the
  explicit-key model degrades **4.64$\times$**; the intrinsic model is
  **bitwise immune** — the input it would have trusted no longer exists.
  This is a permanent demonstration test, not a one-off.
- **The similarity contract is now unconditional**: paired covariance
  2.9–3.1$\times$10$^{-7}$ on trained models, including 0.2$\times$ and
  5$\times$ rescalings, with no convention a caller can break.

One honest bonus, recorded because the discipline found it: the gauge
work flushed out a **latent bitwise-query-independence bug** — the
pair-invariant einsum took a CUDA batched-GEMM path with 1-ulp drift for
any $L \neq 1$, masked until now by test data that always had $L = 1$.
Found, fixed, and noted in the engineering review (@sec-future).

*History: @sec-nb-iter24.*

## Part IV — generalization, stress-tested {#sec-part-generalization}

Generalization was probed **axis by axis** — geometry, topology,
PDE parameter, drive spectrum, query radius, boundary resolution, and
raw scale — with benchmarks designed so that each intended failure mode
has a **control that must fail if the axis is real**. Where the
architecture failed a stress test, the failure was diagnosed to a
mechanism and either fixed by licensed structure or recorded as an open
limit with its number attached. This part holds those suites and their
outcomes.

### The encoder-stress suites: geometry that pair invariants cannot see {#sec-encoder-stress}

These suites (`encoder_stress.py`; their place in the agenda is
@sec-future) exist to test a claim no earlier benchmark could
touch. Every prior 2D suite lives on a (deformed) disk,
where two boundary points close in $\mathbb R^2$ are also close along the
boundary — so a kernel of *pairwise Euclidean invariants* never has to
see around geometry, and the attention encoder's claim to existence
(global boundary-to-boundary information flow before the query decode)
goes untested. Two families close the gap, both with
exterior-point-charge exact labels
($u = \sum_j q_j \log\|x - c_j\|$, charges strictly outside the domain
closure) and unit-RMS boundary traces:

- **Multi-body**: the interior of a circle minus two disjoint disks —
  multiply connected, three Dirichlet boundaries merged into a single
  boundary mesh (identity conveyed geometrically). Some in-disk charges
  are deliberately biased toward the gap-facing surface of their disk,
  so in the narrow-gap regime the trace on the near face of one body is
  dominated by a charge hidden inside the *other* — genuine inter-body
  coupling. The difficulty dial is the surface gap over the sum of disk
  radii; splits: in-distribution, narrow-gap, single-body, and
  unseen-charge-count.
- **Deep cavity**: a simply connected domain whose boundary is a disk
  with a deep, narrow, smoothly filleted slot (a "C-shape"), charges
  nestled *inside the slot* — outside the domain but deep in the cavity
  — so two interior points on opposite cavity walls are Euclidean-close
  while the field between them is mediated by the whole cavity
  geometry. The dial is slot depth over width; splits: in-distribution,
  deep-slot, and a convex control.

```{python}
#| label: fig-stress-multibody
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The multi-body family, one exact case per split, rendered live from
#|   the generator: interior field translucent inside the boundary,
#|   boundary trace emphasized on top (colors per sample, diverging
#|   about the boundary mean). Crosses are the generator's logarithmic
#|   point charges -- exterior to the domain (inside the excluded bodies
#|   or beyond the outer circle), private label-generation state no
#|   model ever sees; exterior charges beyond the crop are not shown. In
#|   the narrow-gap case the hot spot on the near face of each body is
#|   produced by a charge hidden inside the other body -- the inter-body
#|   coupling that pair invariants cannot see.
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.patheffects as mpe
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import torch
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, Normalize

for _entry in (Path("..").resolve(), Path("..").resolve() / "problems"):
    if str(_entry) not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, str(_entry))
from encoder_stress import (
    SPLITS,
    _in_domain,
    build_deep_cavity_sample,
    build_multi_body_sample,
    harmonic_potential,
)

INK, INK2 = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e"
DIVERGING = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "book_diverging", ["#2a78d6", "#f0efec", "#e34948"])


def stress_panel(ax, sample, n_grid=170):
    """Exact interior field on a masked grid, using the generator's own
    domain-membership predicate (winding numbers), chunked for memory."""
    boundary = sample.domain.boundaries["dirichlet"]
    pts = boundary.points.numpy()
    lo, hi = pts.min(axis=0), pts.max(axis=0)
    mid, half = (lo + hi) / 2, (hi - lo).max() / 2 * 1.05
    xs = np.linspace(mid[0] - half, mid[0] + half, n_grid)
    ys = np.linspace(mid[1] - half, mid[1] + half, n_grid)
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    grid_points = torch.tensor(np.stack([X.ravel(), Y.ravel()], axis=1))
    inside = torch.cat([
        _in_domain(sample.boundary_loops, grid_points[i : i + 8192])
        for i in range(0, grid_points.shape[0], 8192)
    ]).numpy()
    values = harmonic_potential(
        grid_points, sample.charge_positions, sample.charge_strengths).numpy()
    field = np.ma.array(values.reshape(n_grid, n_grid),
                        mask=~inside.reshape(n_grid, n_grid))

    trace = boundary.cell_data["boundary_value"].numpy()
    vmid = float(trace.mean())
    amp = max(float(np.abs(field - vmid).max()), float(np.abs(trace - vmid).max()))
    norm = Normalize(vmid - amp, vmid + amp)

    cs = ax.contourf(X, Y, field, levels=np.linspace(vmid - amp, vmid + amp, 27),
                     cmap=DIVERGING, alpha=0.82)
    cs.set_edgecolor("face")
    for hole in sample.boundary_loops[1:]:  # excluded bodies read as solid
        ax.fill(hole[:, 0].numpy(), hole[:, 1].numpy(),
                facecolor="#eae8e1", edgecolor="none", zorder=2)
    segments = boundary.points[boundary.cells].numpy()
    boundary_line = LineCollection(
        segments, colors=DIVERGING(norm(trace)), linewidths=2.2,
        zorder=4, capstyle="round")
    boundary_line.set_path_effects(
        [mpe.Stroke(linewidth=3.0, foreground=INK), mpe.Normal()])
    ax.add_collection(boundary_line)
    charges = sample.charge_positions.numpy()
    keep = (np.abs(charges[:, 0] - mid[0]) < 0.93 * half) & (
        np.abs(charges[:, 1] - mid[1]) < 0.93 * half)
    ax.plot(charges[keep, 0], charges[keep, 1], "x", color=INK, ms=5,
            mew=1.4, zorder=5)
    ax.set_xlim(mid[0] - half, mid[0] + half)
    ax.set_ylim(mid[1] - half, mid[1] + half)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.grid(False)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)


def stress_colorbar(fig, position):
    cax = fig.add_axes(position)
    sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(cmap=DIVERGING, norm=Normalize(-1, 1))
    cbar = fig.colorbar(sm, cax=cax)
    cbar.set_ticks([-1, 0, 1])
    cbar.set_ticklabels(["min", "boundary\nmean", "max"], fontsize=8)
    cbar.set_label("potential $u$ (per sample)", fontsize=9)


cases = [
    ("in_distribution", 3, "in-distribution"),
    ("narrow_gap", 7, "narrow gap"),
    ("single_body", 11, "single body"),
    ("unseen_charge_count", 5, "unseen charge count"),
]
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(9.2, 2.9))
grid = fig.add_gridspec(1, 4, left=0.02, right=0.86, top=0.90, bottom=0.04,
                        wspace=0.06)
for col, (split, seed, label) in enumerate(cases):
    sample = build_multi_body_sample(seed, **SPLITS["multi_body"][split])
    ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, col])
    stress_panel(ax, sample)
    ax.set_title(label, fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
    if not math.isnan(sample.geometry.gap_ratio):
        ax.text(0.5, -0.03, f"gap ratio {sample.geometry.gap_ratio:.2f}",
                transform=ax.transAxes, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=8,
                color=INK2)
stress_colorbar(fig, [0.89, 0.20, 0.018, 0.60])
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-stress-cavity
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The deep-cavity family, same rendering conventions as the
#|   multi-body gallery. Charges (crosses) nestled inside the slot are
#|   outside the domain but deep in the cavity, so opposite slot walls
#|   are Euclidean-close while the exact field between them -- the plume
#|   filling the slot -- is mediated by the whole cavity geometry. The
#|   difficulty dial is slot depth over width; the convex control
#|   (right) is the same generator at zero slot depth.
# Reuses stress_panel/stress_colorbar from the multi-body cell above
# (same kernel session).
cases = [
    ("in_distribution", 3, "in-distribution"),
    ("deep_slot", 7, "deep slot"),
    ("convex_control", 11, "convex control"),
]
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7.2, 2.9))
grid = fig.add_gridspec(1, 3, left=0.02, right=0.84, top=0.90, bottom=0.04,
                        wspace=0.06)
for col, (split, seed, label) in enumerate(cases):
    sample = build_deep_cavity_sample(seed, **SPLITS["deep_cavity"][split])
    ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, col])
    stress_panel(ax, sample, n_grid=200)
    ax.set_title(label, fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
    g = sample.geometry
    if g.slot_depth > 0:
        ax.text(0.5, -0.03,
                f"depth/width {g.slot_depth / (2 * g.slot_half_width):.1f}",
                transform=ax.transAxes, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=8,
                color=INK2)
stress_colorbar(fig, [0.875, 0.20, 0.022, 0.60])
plt.show()
```

Every generated sample is **certified at build time**: cell-orientation
winding numbers place all queries inside and all charges outside, charge
standoff from the discretized boundary is checked numerically, the
cavity curve passes an exact all-pairs segment-intersection test, and
the multi-body boundaries are verified disjoint. The **free-form pair
kernel is the load-bearing control**: it is exactly the model class that
sees only pair invariants, so any split where it fails and an
encoder-bearing model succeeds is direct evidence for global boundary
coupling. One honest caveat from the suite's validation: the families
are a *separation dial*, not a binary proof — the construction makes
pair invariants blind to the coupling, but how much that blindness
costs is an empirical question the control answers, not a theorem.

### The 3D suite {#sec-3d-suite}

The 3D suite extends the methodology across dimension
(`laplace3d.py`; built as a direct test of the `Mesh` module's dimensional
genericity — subdivided-icosahedron triangle meshes with `cell_areas`,
`cell_normals`, `cell_centroids` from the same code paths as 2D).

![The 3D geometry tiers, colored by exact Dirichlet data from exterior point
charges. T1: randomized spheres (radius, center, orientation). T2:
star-shaped $Y_{lm}$ radial deformations — new curvature, same topology. T3:
spherical shells — multiply connected, two boundaries that may carry
different BC types; the cutaway (camera-facing half of the outer boundary
removed) shows the interior boundary. Rendered from the generator's surface
and manufactured-solution components; the star row bypasses the
interior-query sampler, which currently hangs (see the engineering review,
@sec-future).](figures/gallery_3d.png){#fig-gallery3d}

**Tiers** vary shape *and* connectivity:

- **T1 sphere** — random radius $\in [0.7, 1.5]$, center, and mesh
  orientation; the calibration tier.
- **T2 star** — $r(\hat u) = R\,(1 + \sum \varepsilon\, Y_{lm}(\hat u))$ over
  low-degree real spherical harmonics, with held-out degree-4 modes for
  geometry-OOD; homeomorphic to the sphere but with varied curvature.
- **T3 shell** — an outer boundary plus an inward-oriented inner boundary;
  multiply connected, with cavity charges so the solution has genuinely
  multiply-connected structure. The pure double-layer ansatz is
  rank-deficient here, which is precisely why this tier is *declared
  unsolved* for the first 3D model generation rather than quietly excluded.

**BC regimes**, always well-posed (@sec-pde-theory): all-Dirichlet; mixed
(exactly one boundary keeps Dirichlet, the other carries the dimensionless
flux $L\,\partial_n u$); Robin with per-boundary $\beta \in [0.2, 2]$.
All-Neumann is excluded by construction.

**The first 3D model** carries the 2D lessons across dimension: the pruned
flagship's analogue — a $c_1$ double-layer coefficient with the **exact
triangle quadrature** given in closed form by the van Oosterom–Strackee
signed solid angle (`solid_angle_influence`,
$\int_{T} n\cdot(y-x)/(4\pi|y-x|^3)\,dS = -\Omega/4\pi$), a shared-$\alpha$
$p{=}8$ Richardson solve in the orientation gauge that keeps zero-kernel
initialization convergent, and 2 parameters total — benchmarked on
all-Dirichlet T1/T2 in the next section, with T3 the declared open tier for
a mixed-trace/Green-representation learned solve (parked with the
specialist line; @sec-future).

### 3D results {#sec-3d-results}

All numbers in this section are seed-17 session artifacts (`/tmp/h5_3d*`),
evaluated on frozen 12-case banks per split.

Two rows anchor the table. The **oracle** is parameter-free: the exact
solid-angle influence with a dense solve of the second-kind system — the
best any double-layer representation can do at this panel resolution. The
**learned model** is `SolidAngleBIE`: *two* parameters (one kernel
coefficient multiplying the exact solid-angle influence, one shared
Richardson relaxation, eight solve steps), with **no reference frame at
all** — solid angles are dimensionless and similarity-invariant by
construction, so the 2D nondimensionalization machinery disappears entirely.

| split | learned 2-param (10k steps) | dense-solve oracle |
|---|--:|--:|
| sphere (T1) | 0.0041 | 0.0041 |
| star (T2) | 0.0023 | 0.0024 |
| star, unseen deformation modes | 0.0024 | 0.0021 |
| shell (T3, topology) | 0.2764 | 1.1348 |

: 3D all-Dirichlet relative $L^2$; the learned model matches the oracle to
within $3\times10^{-4}$ on every simply connected split. No PDE-residual
column is needed here: both rows propagate the exact solid-angle kernel, so
their strong-form residual is float-noise zero *by construction* on every
split (the driver's fidelity block, @sec-fidelity-columns, measures
$\sim$$10^{-14}$). {#tbl-3d}

Three observations:

1. **Learning converges to the oracle.** The learned kernel coefficient
   reaches $-1.0029$ against the gauge-consistent value $-1$ (0.3%), and
   validation is flat from step 9,000: accuracy on T1/T2 is now
   quadrature-limited, not learning-limited. The 2D story — recover the
   analytic kernel from interior data alone — repeats in 3D with even fewer
   parameters, and with the same slow co-adaptation transit seen on 2D
   Neumann (1,500 steps reach only 0.50; 10,000 are needed).
2. **The shell tier fails for a classical reason, in both rows.** A pure
   double-layer representation is incomplete on multiply connected domains;
   the *oracle itself* scores 1.13. This is a representation fact, not a
   learning failure, and it is exactly the gap a mixed-trace/Green-representation
   solve would close (parked with the specialist line; @sec-future).
3. **Truncated solves regularize.** The learned model *beats* the oracle on
   shells (0.28 vs 1.13): eight Richardson steps cannot fully invert the
   deficient system, and that truncation acts as implicit (Landweber-style)
   spectral regularization, while the dense solve inverts the pathology
   faithfully. The tier remains open — but the mechanism is worth keeping in
   mind wherever a learned unrolled solve meets an ill-posed representation.

The 3D build also stress-tested the `Mesh` module's dimensional genericity,
which held: codimension-one triangle areas, outward normals, and centroids
in 3D worked unchanged, and interior solid-angle row sums came out exactly
$-1$. One generator bug (an over-loose analytic bound that hung the star
tier's rejection sampler) was caught by *figure inspection* during the
gallery work and fixed with empirical per-surface radial bounds.

#### The full architecture in 3D {#sec-3d-meshtransformer}

The kernel-decoder `MeshTransformer` trains on the 3D suite with **zero
core changes** and a **bitwise-identical parameter count** to 2D (channel
counts are dimension-independent). The only new code is example-level glue

merged into a single `dirichlet` boundary, so boundary identity is conveyed

### The screened suite through the full architecture {#sec-screened}

The parametric study answered the basis-versus-conditioning question with
specialist pair-kernel BIEs on the screened Laplace (modified Helmholtz)
family $\Delta u - \kappa^2 u = 0$ (@sec-parametric). The same benchmark
also runs through the *full generalist architecture*: the kernel-decoder
`MeshTransformer`, with the dimensionless parameter
$\tilde\kappa = \kappa R$ entering **only** as an operator-side global
scalar (`screening`) — it conditions the operator encoder, and through it
the kernel-decoder coefficients. The field mode stays `linear`: the PDE is
drive-linear, so the superposition contract is kept. Two arms — 8 MLP
members (110,593 parameters) versus dictionary-only (105,121) — three
seeds (17/18/19), 2,000 steps, the same protocol as the @sec-parametric
specialists they are compared against (checked-in key
`iteration_9_screened_meshtransformer`; the best current arm,
singular-only, is in @sec-singonly-universality). The framing rule matters
most here: the specialists *know the PDE* — their kernel bases are exact
Yukawa fundamental solutions — while the `MeshTransformer` is handed the
number $\tilde\kappa$ but not its meaning.

What this establishes — the specialist–generalist trade, measured
honestly. In distribution, the generalist beats the harmonic-basis
specialist by $\sim$5$\times$ (mean ID 0.012 versus 0.061) *without
knowing the PDE*, and stays within $\sim$4$\times$ of the
exact-Yukawa-basis specialists (0.003–0.0005) that *do* know it.
Parameter-OOD splits the ledger in two, and the asymmetry is the finding:

- **High $\tilde\kappa$: the exact basis wins decisively** (0.016 versus
  0.18) — the expected price of not knowing the equation; conditioning
  does not extrapolate the parameter, only analytic structure does.
- **Low $\tilde\kappa$: the Yukawa-basis specialists diverge
  catastrophically** (8.7–28, as $K_0$ diverges logarithmically for
  $\tilde\kappa \to 0$) **while the `MeshTransformer` degrades gracefully
  to 0.03–0.05** — its harmonic-biased singular dictionary already
  *contains* the $\tilde\kappa \to 0$ limit.

That asymmetry is the **graceful-degradation argument** for
harmonic-biased dictionaries in the unknown-PDE product setting: a
specialist basis fails catastrophically outside its asymptotic regime; a
dictionary containing the benign limit buys bounded degradation where the
exact basis cannot go. The PDE-residual columns keep the trade honest in
both directions: the generalist's 0.49–0.68 sits squarely between the
exact-basis specialists' exact 0 and the wrong-basis conditioner's 1.65 —
its excellent ID numbers are earned by fitting the field, not by
satisfying the screened operator, and the column now says so in the same
table as the $L^2$ scores. The suite
also delivered the strongest dictionary-selection replication of the
linear-PDE pattern: MLP members leave ID and both $\tilde\kappa$-OOD
splits unchanged but destroy unseen-modes generalization 10$\times$
(0.184 vs 0.019, 3/3 seeds; @sec-dictionary-selection).

### The far-field ladder: strong inference, start to finish {#sec-farfield-ladder}

The far-field split — every potential-flow arm degrading on queries
beyond the training annulus — resisted two architectural generations
(@sec-fluid-suites) before falling to a four-rung falsification ladder.
The arc is this program's method in miniature: rival mechanisms with
pre-registered discriminators, a fix that refuted its own diagnosis
instructively, a construction that excluded the leading mechanism
outright, and licensed exact structure to finish. Archive keys
`iteration_27_farfield_strong_inference` through
`iteration_30_decay_structure` (with `five_seed_close`); session
artifacts `farfield_inference*.json` in `results/`.

**Rung 1 — strong inference (three rivals, pre-registered
discriminators).** **M1, annulus coverage: partial.** Widening the
training annulus $[1.05, 4] \to [1.05, 8]$ cuts far-field 0.694 $\to$
0.179 (74%) — but the model stays 6.2$\times$ above ID *inside* the new
annulus: strong mitigation, not the cause. **M2, member decay:
excluded.** The member basis is exactly analytic on $[4, 12]$
(double-layer exponent $-1.9$; single-layer $+1/\ln r$), while the
prediction *super*-decays (exponent $-24$ against the exact $-2$) — the
wrong direction for member tails; a basis that cannot out-decay $r^{-2}$
cannot host this pathology. **M3, coefficient extrapolation: supported,
with a smoking gun.** The output-projection sigmoid gate collapses at
the training edge — 0.52 at $r = 1.1$, 0.010 at $r = 4$,
$2.3\times10^{-17}$ at $r = 12$ — and, out of sample, the collapse onset
**moves with the training annulus** on the annulus-8 checkpoint: the
pathology tracks the training boundary, not the dictionary. One process
note, disclosed: M2's verdict as first coded implemented only the
magnitude half of its pre-registered rule; the *directional* qualifier
(written in the docstring before measurement) is what flips it to
excluded — and the annulus-8 edge-tracking corroborates M3
independently.

**Rung 2 — the gate fix, refuted instructively.** Bounding the gate
inputs worked exactly as designed (smooth nonzero gate, no saturation
regime) — and far-field got **4.3$\times$ worse** (0.694 $\to$ 2.98).
The collapse was **load-bearing**: it had been suppressing polynomially
growing query-side direct-drive branches (a lifted-drive branch grows
0.026 at $r = 1.1$ to 1.45 at $r = 12$; drive norms grow like
$r$–$r^2$). The corrected root cause is the *pair* of unbounded radial
dependences — a saturating gate **and** growing linear branches — not
either alone. Silver lining, kept: bounded gates improve in-annulus
accuracy (ID 0.0215 vs 0.0269, circulation-OOD 0.018 vs 0.033).

**Rung 3 — bound at the source.** Compactify the *injected query
position* ($x \to x/\sqrt{1+|x|^2}$, equivariant), so every learned
coefficient sees bounded invariants — with the kernel members verified
**bitwise-pinned to raw positions**, keeping the physics path exact.
This excludes M3 *by construction* (coefficient traces flat to
$r = 12$; far/near ratio 1.03), and far-field lands at 0.452. The
residual is thereby isolated as purely **representational**: bounded is
not decaying — the direct part converges to a direction-dependent
constant (exponent $\approx 0$) where the exact field decays $r^{-2}$,
and the single-layer $\log r$ tail is fit only by near-cancellation
in-annulus.

**Rung 4 — decay structure, licensed and exact.** Two structures the
physics licenses for zero-net-flux exteriors, zero parameters added:
an exact $r^{-2}$ **direct-drive envelope** ($1/(1+|x|^2)$ — the
leading order of a 2D exterior zero-flux velocity field is the doublet,
and the direct drive may not outlive it), and **monopole-free
single-layer deflation** — a measure-weighted rank-one deflation of the
single-layer member column giving exact zero net charge per member, so
the $\log r$ tail is dead *for any coefficients*. A corollary worth its
sentence: the 2D log gauge cancels under the deflation, so the deflated
member is exactly similarity invariant.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The far-field ladder (checked-in learned_bie_2026-07-02.json,
#|   iterations 27-30; log scale). Per-rung far-field relative L2, with
#|   the iteration-28 regression shown as the honest spike: the gate fix
#|   worked as designed and made things 4.3x worse, correcting the
#|   diagnosis. Rung 4 shows the five-seed close (small dots = seeds
#|   17-21; large dot = mean 0.090), crossing the pre-registered
#|   fully-fixed bar at the mean with two seeds above it.
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

results = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "learned_bie_2026-07-02.json"))
it28 = results["iteration_28_bounded_gate"]["measured"]
it29 = results["iteration_29_source_bounded_query"]["measured"]
close = results["iteration_30_decay_structure"]["five_seed_close"]

rungs = [
    ("baseline\n(rung 1: diagnosed)", it28["baseline_farfield"], "#eda100",
     "gate collapse found"),
    ("bounded gate\n(rung 2: refuted)", it28["farfield"], "#e34948",
     "collapse was load-bearing"),
    ("source-bounded\n(rung 3: M3 excluded)", it29["farfield"], "#2a78d6",
     "residual is representational"),
    ("+ decay structure\n(rung 4: closed)", close["means"]["farfield"],
     "#1baf7a", "licensed exact physics"),
]
seeds4 = [run["farfield_queries"] for run in close["runs"]]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 4.2))
ax.axhline(0.10, color="#0b0b0b", lw=1.2, ls="--")
ax.text(-0.42, 0.104, "pre-registered fully-fixed bar (0.10)", fontsize=8,
        color="#0b0b0b", va="bottom")
ax.plot(range(4), [r[1] for r in rungs], "-", color="#c3c2b7", lw=1.4,
        zorder=1)
for i, (label, value, color, verdict) in enumerate(rungs):
    ax.plot(i, value, "o", ms=10, color=color, mec="white", mew=1.4,
            zorder=3)
    ax.annotate(f"{value:.3g}\n{verdict}", (i, value),
                textcoords="offset points",
                xytext=(0, 12 if i != 2 else -34), ha="center", fontsize=8,
                color="#52514e")
ax.plot([3 + 0.07 * (j - 2) for j in range(5)], seeds4, "o", ms=5,
        color="#1baf7a", mec="white", mew=1.0, alpha=0.75, zorder=2)
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xticks(range(4), [r[0] for r in rungs])
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 3.5)
ax.set_ylim(0.02, 8.0)
ax.set_ylabel("far-field relative $L^2$ (log)")
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

**The five-seed close.** Far-field mean **0.090 ± 0.048** — the
pre-registered fully-fixed bar ($< 0.10$) crossed at the mean, with the
per-seed spread stated honestly: 0.036–0.147, two seeds above 0.10.
That is **7.7$\times$ at an unchanged training annulus**, beating the
coverage lever (0.179 from doubling the annulus), and every other split
lands at family-best levels:

| decay-structure config (5 seeds) | ID | circulation-OOD | unseen geometry | wilder shapes | far-field |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| per-seed far-field | | | | | 0.036 / 0.061 / 0.074 / 0.133 / 0.147 |
| **means** | **0.0174** | **0.0168** | **0.0303** | 0.116 | **0.090 ± 0.048** |

: The ladder's endpoint: the four physics-licensed knobs (bounded gate,
bounded query source, $r^{-2}$ envelope, monopole-free single layer)
compose into a strictly dominant configuration. {#tbl-farfield-close}

The takeaway is the program's motto in action: the learned coefficients
were made **bounded** — trust nothing learned beyond its data — and all
far-field radial physics was moved into **exact, licensed structure**.
One leak remains fitted rather than exact — the $r^{-1}$ member tails
cancel to $r^{-2}$ only through learned zero-circulation cancellation —
and it is the recorded residual (@sec-future).

*History: @sec-nb-iter27 through @sec-nb-iter30.*

### The scale ladder: measured cost curves, and the wall named {#sec-scale}

The cost law is the designed one, inference already fits a single A100
at the product scope, and the wall is training memory — named, with two
characterized fixes. The study was sequenced after simplification on
purpose (@sec-future), and it runs against the
simplified model: `scale_study.py` measures the 3D `singpair` arm at
`operator_layers=1` (81,961 parameters — the depth @sec-mixed-bc showed
sufficient) on an A100 80GB. Two instruments: a **cost grid** of
320–20,480 boundary triangles $\times$ $10^3$–$10^5$ queries,
OOM-guarded, with encode and decode timed separately; and
**resolution-transfer** training at subdivisions 2 with zero-shot
evaluation at subdivisions 2/3/4. Checked-in key
`iteration_20_scale_ladder`.

**The cost law is the designed one.**

| quantity (power-law fit over the grid) | fitted law | $R^2$ |
|---|---|--:|
| decode time | $\propto Q^{0.97}\,S^{0.96}$ | 0.999 |
| forward time | $\propto Q^{0.89}\,S^{0.87}$ | 0.988 |
| encode time | flat over the range ($S^{0.11}$; launch-dominated) | 0.62 |
| forward peak memory | $\propto S^{0.95}\,Q^{0.16}$ | 0.988 |
| training peak memory | $\propto S^{0.95}\,Q^{0.44}$ | 0.997 |

: A100 cost-grid fits (12 grid points per timing fit; $Q$ = queries,
$S$ = boundary cells). {#tbl-scale-fits}

The decode fits $O(Q^{0.97} S^{0.96})$ at $R^2 = 0.999$ — the
documented dense $O(N_qN_s)$, measured rather than assumed. The encoder
shows **no growth with boundary size over the measured range**: the
separable-moment encoder is $O(N_s)$ per layer, the measurements are
kernel-launch-overhead dominated, and the fitted $S^{0.11}$ is a floor
artifact — the encoder is explicitly *not* the wall.

**The wall, stated honestly.** Extrapolated to the product scope
($10^5$ boundary cells $\times$ $10^6$ queries — an extrapolation
roughly an order of magnitude beyond the measured grid, not a
measurement), **training memory breaks first**: one forward+backward
$\approx$ **742 GiB**, 9$\times$ an 80-GiB A100, because autograd
retains the dense $O(N_qN_s)$ pair activations of the kernel decode.
The two named fixes have different characters: **gradient checkpointing
over query chunks** — exact and cheap, recomputing the pair features in
the backward pass — or a **hierarchical decode backend** (FMM-style) —
approximate but classical, with the dense implementation retained as
the oracle. Inference is already inside a single A100 with query
chunking: $\approx$85 GB (79.4 GiB) peak, at roughly **9–16 minutes per
forward** at product scope (fitted forward 541 s; fitted dense decode
956 s). One fit is suppressed in the archive, with reasons recorded:
the forward+backward *time* extrapolation fell below forward-only (the
surviving small grid points are overhead-dominated on this device), so
the ideal $O(N_qN_s)$ projection from the largest measured point
($\approx$1,355 s) stands in for it.

**Resolution transfer at scale.** The exact-quadrature transfer claim,
now at 3D scale: trained at subdivisions 2, evaluated zero-shot across a
16$\times$ range of boundary resolution —

| tier | subdiv 2 (trained) | subdiv 3 | subdiv 4 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| sphere | 0.0101 | 0.0155 | 0.0175 |
| star | 0.0136 | 0.0196 | 0.0312 |

: Zero-shot resolution transfer, relative $L^2$ (fully trained model).
{#tbl-scale-transfer}

— the claim holds with mild degradation: no retraining, no collapse,
under a 16$\times$ change in discretization.

One profiling find, engineering hygiene rather than research:
`PairInvariantFeatures` currently computes unconditionally in the dense
hot loop even when the dictionary has no smooth members to consume it —
roughly ten dead floats per pair on the flagship singular-only and
singpair arms. A straightforward speed fix (@sec-future).

### The wall, broken {#sec-scale-ckpt}

The training-memory wall named above is now **measured closed**. The
exact fix — `kernel_checkpoint_query_chunks`, backward-pass
recomputation of each decode chunk's dense pair activations
(@sec-decoder-role; bitwise identical outputs and gradients, by test) —
was run against the retained-graph default in a paired measurement:
same GB200, same seed, same per-point samples, identical protocol.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scale-ckpt
#| output: asis
import json
from pathlib import Path

paired = json.load(
    open(Path("..") / "results" / "scale_checkpoint_paired_2026-07-05.json")
)
GB = 1024.0**3


def grid_rows(report):
    rows = {}
    for g in report["cost"]["grid"]:
        rows[(g["n_boundary_cells"], g["n_query"])] = g
    return rows


dense = grid_rows(paired["dense"])
ckpt = grid_rows(paired["checkpointed"])
lines = [
    "| boundary cells $\\times$ queries | dense train peak | checkpointed "
    "train peak | step-time ratio |",
    "|---|--:|--:|--:|",
]
for key in sorted(ckpt):
    d, c = dense.get(key, {}), ckpt[key]
    if d.get("train_peak_bytes"):
        dtxt = f"{d['train_peak_bytes'] / GB:.1f} GiB"
    else:
        dtxt = "**OOM** (189 GB)"
    ctxt = f"{c['train_peak_bytes'] / GB:.1f} GiB"
    dfb = (d.get("forward_backward_ms") or {}).get("median_ms")
    cfb = (c.get("forward_backward_ms") or {}).get("median_ms")
    ratio = f"{cfb / dfb:.1f}$\\times$" if (dfb and cfb) else "—"
    lines.append(
        f"| {key[0]:,} $\\times$ {key[1]:,} | {dtxt} | {ctxt} | {ratio} |"
    )
lines.append(
    ": Paired training-memory measurement, GB200, seed 17, identical "
    "samples per point (archive: `scale_checkpoint_paired_2026-07-05."
    "json`). {#tbl-scale-ckpt-paired}"
)
print("\n".join(lines))
```

Three facts carry the section's conclusion. The checkpointed peak is
essentially **query-count-independent at fixed boundary size** — the
designed behavior, since only one chunk's activations plus the outputs
are ever retained. The near-product corner (81,920 boundary cells
$\times$ $10^6$ queries), where the dense graph OOMs a 189 GB device
and extrapolates to the terabyte scale, **trains in 71.4 GiB — inside
a single 80 GiB-class accelerator**. And the price is a consistent
$\approx$1.9$\times$ step time (the recomputed decode forward inside
backward), with the operator, outputs, and gradients bitwise unchanged.
Agenda item 2 of @sec-future is thereby closed; the hierarchical decode
backend remains as the (approximate) speed lever, not a memory
necessity.

*History: @sec-nb-iter20, @sec-nb-industrial-pivot.*

## Part V — against the strongest mainstream baseline {#sec-part-baseline}

A steel-manned **Transolver** — given *more* interaction than the
MeshTransformer gets — loses in both its regimes and ours: 20$\times$
at matched budget streaming, 7.7$\times$ on its own fixed-dataset home
turf, and up to 78$\times$ on the smooth parametric and 3D tiers —
narrowing to 1.4$\times$ on the shell tier, exactly where the
MeshTransformer is itself representation-limited. The two gaps
that never close with budget — drive-spectrum extrapolation and exact
equivariance — are exactly the two things the architecture declares
rather than learns.

### The Transolver comparison: the thesis ablation {#sec-transolver}

The program's first mainstream-baseline comparison, run as **the ablation
of the program's thesis** — what does building boundary-integral
structure into attention buy, and at what cost?

**Setup, honestly.** The baseline is a faithful port of **Transolver**
(Wu et al., ICML 2024, arXiv
[2402.02366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02366)) — the strongest
physics-agnostic attention architecture for PDE surrogacy — verified
against the official implementation, with steel-man adaptations to the
boundary$\to$interior problem shape: a *shared boundary+query token
sequence*, which gives Transolver **more** interaction than the
`MeshTransformer` gets (its queries attend to each other; ours are
independent by contract), and identical normalization to our baselines.
The training protocol is identical to every `MeshTransformer` run:
streaming generation (one fresh case per step), AdamW $3\times10^{-4}$,
seeds 17/29/43, the frozen reference banks. Two capacities: **matched**
(103,053 parameters, against singular-only's 104,261) and **native**
(2,809,409 — 27$\times$). Checked-in key
`iteration_15_transolver_comparison`.

| model | params | steps | ID (3-seed mean) | freq-OOD | sim. covariance | PDE residual |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Transolver, matched | 103,053 | 3,000 | 0.769 | 1.00 | 0.06–0.13 | — |
| Transolver, native | 2,809,409 | 3,000 | 0.608 | 0.97 | 0.10–0.25 | — |
| Transolver, native | 2,809,409 | 10,000 | 0.262 | 0.77 | 0.18–0.21 | — |
| Transolver, native | 2,809,409 | 30,000 | 0.119 | 0.46 | 0.08–0.11 | — |
| **MeshTransformer, singular-only** | 104,261 | 3,000 | **0.0375** | **0.0748** | **3$\times$10$^{-7}$** | — |

: The Transolver comparison on the frozen 2D reference banks; similarity
covariance is measured on the trained checkpoints (archived per-run
`sim_cov` fields). The PDE-residual column is em-dashed: these archived
runs predate fidelity-first reporting (@sec-fidelity-columns).
{#tbl-transolver}

```{python}
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The step curve of the thesis ablation (checked-in
#|   learned_bie_2026-07-02.json, iteration 15; log-log). Red: Transolver
#|   at native capacity (2.8M params, 27x), one line per seed. Yellow
#|   dots: Transolver at matched capacity (103k) at 3,000 steps. Dashed
#|   line: the MeshTransformer singular-only reference (104k params,
#|   3,000 steps, ID 0.0375). After 10x the compute and 27x the
#|   parameters, native Transolver remains 3.2x above the reference; the
#|   power-law slope suggests ~300k+ steps to close the ID gap alone.
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

results = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "learned_bie_2026-07-02.json"))
it15 = results["iteration_15_transolver_comparison"]
native = {17: [], 29: [], 43: []}
matched = []
for run in it15["runs_3000"] + it15["runs_step_curve"]:
    if run["parameters"] > 1_000_000:
        native[run["seed"]].append((run["steps"], run["ID"]))
    else:
        matched.append((run["steps"], run["ID"]))
reference = it15["reference_MT_singonly_3000steps"]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.0))
for seed, points in native.items():
    points.sort()
    ax.plot([p[0] for p in points], [p[1] for p in points], "o-",
            color="#e34948", lw=1.6, ms=6, mec="white", mew=1.0,
            label="Transolver, native (2.8M)" if seed == 17 else None)
# Slight multiplicative x-jitter so the three near-identical matched
# seed values (0.757-0.781) remain individually visible on the log axis.
for jitter, (steps, value) in zip((0.93, 1.0, 1.08), matched):
    ax.plot(steps * jitter, value, "o", color="#eda100", ms=8,
            mec="white", mew=1.2,
            label="Transolver, matched (103k)" if jitter == 1.0 else None)
ax.axhline(reference["ID"], color="#1baf7a", lw=1.8, ls="--",
           label="MeshTransformer singular-only (104k), 3k steps")
ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xlim(2.2e3, 4.5e4)
ax.set_ylim(0.02, 1.2)
ax.set_xlabel("online training steps (log)")
ax.set_ylabel("ID relative $L^2$ (log)")
ax.grid(True, color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper right", frameon=False)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Three findings, in decreasing order of negotiability:

1. **Data efficiency: 20$\times$ at matched everything.** At matched
   parameters and compute, Transolver reaches ID 0.769 against 0.0375.
   At native capacity the step curve descends 0.608 $\to$ 0.262 $\to$
   0.119 over 3k/10k/30k steps: after 10$\times$ the compute and
   27$\times$ the parameters, still 3.2$\times$ worse than the
   `MeshTransformer` at 3k. The power-law slope suggests $\sim$300k+
   steps to close the ID gap alone. This gap is *expected* to be
   closable with data and compute; that is what makes it the negotiable
   one.
2. **Frequency-OOD does not train away.** Native freq-OOD saturates
   around 0.46 at 30k steps (against 0.0748): physics-agnostic attention
   interpolates the drive distribution it has seen and does not
   extrapolate the drive spectrum — the same signature the free-form
   pair kernel and the full-dictionary decoder showed
   (@sec-dictionary-selection), now measured on the strongest mainstream
   representative of the class.
3. **The equivariance gap is architectural.** Similarity covariance on
   trained Transolver checkpoints sits at 0.08–0.25 across *every*
   capacity and step budget — it does not improve with training — while
   the trained `MeshTransformer` measures $3\times10^{-7}$: five to six
   orders of magnitude, by construction rather than by data. A rotated,
   translated, or rescaled copy of a problem is the *same problem* to
   one architecture and a new problem to the other.

::: {.callout-warning title="Scope"}
Both fairness regimes are tested — the streaming small-data regime above
(this program's claimed strength) and Transolver's own published regime
below (@sec-transolver-dataset) — so the steel-man is complete.
Transolver still retains genuine advantages outside this benchmark's
scope: volumetric and piecewise inputs (its native habitat, which the
boundary-only `MeshTransformer` cannot ingest at all), and linear $O(N)$
attention at industrial $N$, where the kernel decoder's dense
$O(N_qN_s)$ decode is measured and gated in @sec-scale. What the
comparison establishes is the thesis ablation: on boundary-driven
problems, the BIE structure — equivariance, quadrature, drive linearity,
exact singularity — is worth 7.7–20$\times$ at matched budget depending
on regime, and two of its properties (drive-spectrum extrapolation and
exact equivariance) are not reachable by scaling the physics-agnostic
baseline at any budget tested.
:::

## Part VI — solver-labeled viscous flow: the ledge {#sec-part-ns}

The evaluation discipline survives contact with a **real solver**:
Navier–Stokes labels from a certified FEM solve, with measured
label-noise floors reported per case, and the contract story carries
over — the pressure wall becomes a *function of Reynolds number*, graded
exactly as the physics grades the nonlinearity. This part is the
program's current frontier.

### Navier–Stokes: the first solver-labeled viscous suite {#sec-ns-cavity}

**The evaluation discipline survives contact with a real solver, and
the contract story becomes Reynolds-graded.** Every ground truth so far
was either closed-form (harmonic constructions, Bessel series, exact
Euler flows) or, in the FEM catalog, a *linear* solve; this suite's
labels come from a numerical solver on a genuinely **nonlinear** PDE —
steady incompressible Navier–Stokes at moderate Reynolds number,

$$
-\nu\,\Delta u + (u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p = 0,
\qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,
$$

with Dirichlet velocity boundary conditions on the bank's certified
star domains. That changes the *epistemic status of every declared
structure*: on the exact Euler suites, drive-linearity of the velocity
and drive-degree-2 of the pressure were facts of the physics that the
architecture could declare as contracts. For Navier–Stokes the solution
map is analytic in the drive with **all** polynomial orders present —
the Stokes component is drive-linear, each convection correction raises
the degree — so the declared-degree arm becomes an approximation
hypothesis, the linear arm's wall becomes a *function of Reynolds
number* rather than an all-or-nothing barrier, and the labels
themselves carry a noise floor that must be measured and reported.
Suite artifacts: `results/ns_solver_verification_2026-07-05.json`
(solver credential), `results/ns_cavity_star_2026-07-05.json` (dataset
and arms), archive key `iteration_36_navier_stokes`.

**The family** (`ns_cavity_star`, generated by
`datasets/generate_datasets.py`, solved by
`datasets/fem_navier_stokes.py`). Star-deformed disks from the bank's
geometry family carry a smooth, band-limited **tangential** boundary
velocity localized on a boundary arc — a driven lid bent around a
smooth cavity. Tangential-only is the load-bearing choice: the drive
has zero normal flux *pointwise*, so the incompressibility
compatibility condition $\oint u\cdot n\,ds = 0$ holds exactly at the
continuous level by construction, and the small discrete defect of the
interpolated trace (reported per case, typically $10^{-6}$) is absorbed
by the mean-pressure gauge multiplier rather than poisoning the solve.
The profile is a $C^\infty$ bump on a random arc (25–50% of the
perimeter) times a band-limited Fourier modulation, normalized to unit
peak speed — so with unit reference length, $\mathrm{Re} = 1/\nu$
exactly, and the global operator scalar fed to every arm is the PDE
coefficient $\tilde\nu = 1/\mathrm{Re}$ (the screened-suite
convention). Splits: `train`/`eval_id` at $\mathrm{Re} \in [10, 200]$
(log-uniform), `eval_unseen_Re` at $(200, 300]$, `eval_unseen_geometry`
at the bank's 0.45–0.65 deformation range, and
`eval_unseen_drive_profile` with modulation modes 3–5 against the
training 0–2. Targets are the velocity (rank 1) and pressure (rank 0)
at 128 interior queries (wall distance $\ge 0.12$) plus a 32-query
**near-wall bucket** (distance 0.02–0.08) — the boundary-layer
diagnostic, stored with per-query wall distances.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ns-hero
#| fig-cap: >
#|   One production case of ns_cavity_star (geometry seed 3, Re = 200,
#|   production mesh). Left: the tangential drive profile on the
#|   boundary, in normalized arc length -- a smooth bump-windowed
#|   band-limited lid, zero on most of the boundary, unit peak speed.
#|   Middle: velocity magnitude of the Taylor-Hood solution (P2, shown
#|   on the mesh); the driven arc throws a wall jet that rolls into a
#|   cavity-scale recirculation. Right: pressure (P1, zero-mean gauge)
#|   with the stagnation-pressure structure at the arc's ends. This is
#|   the field the models must reconstruct from 64 boundary panels, the
#|   drive, and one scalar.
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.tri as mtri
import numpy as np

hero = np.load(Path("data") / "ns_hero_case_2026-07-05.npz")
loop = hero["loop"]
n_vertices = hero["vertex_pressure"].shape[0]
tri = mtri.Triangulation(
    hero["node_points"][:n_vertices, 0], hero["node_points"][:n_vertices, 1],
    triangles=hero["triangles"],
)
speed = np.linalg.norm(hero["node_velocity"], axis=1)[:n_vertices]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10.2, 3.5),
                         gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.0, 1.15, 1.15]})
ax = axes[0]
ax.plot(hero["arc_fraction"], hero["drive_profile"], color="#0b0b0b", lw=1.4)
ax.axhline(0.0, color="#e1e0d9", lw=1.0, zorder=0)
ax.set_xlabel("normalized arc length $s/L$ [-]")
ax.set_ylabel("tangential drive $g(s)$ [-]")
ax.set_title(f"drive profile (Re = {float(hero['reynolds']):.0f})",
             fontsize=9)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)

ax = axes[1]
im = ax.tripcolor(tri, speed, shading="gouraud", cmap="viridis",
                  rasterized=True)
ax.plot(np.append(loop[:, 0], loop[0, 0]), np.append(loop[:, 1], loop[0, 1]),
        color="#0b0b0b", lw=0.8)
ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_axis_off()
ax.set_title("velocity magnitude $|u|$ [-]", fontsize=9)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8, pad=0.02)

ax = axes[2]
im = ax.tripcolor(tri, hero["vertex_pressure"],
                  shading="gouraud", cmap="RdBu_r", rasterized=True)
ax.plot(np.append(loop[:, 0], loop[0, 0]), np.append(loop[:, 1], loop[0, 1]),
        color="#0b0b0b", lw=0.8)
ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_axis_off()
ax.set_title("pressure $p$ (zero-mean gauge) [-]", fontsize=9)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8, pad=0.02)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

#### The label credential {#sec-ns-verification}

A solver-labeled suite is only as good as its labels, and model errors
around $10^{-2}$ demand labels an order better. The solver is a
Taylor–Hood P2–P1 finite-element discretization (inf-sup stable;
velocity $O(h^3)$, pressure $O(h^2)$) with exact-Jacobian Newton, a
Stokes initial guess, backtracking, and a warm-started viscosity
continuation ladder; the pressure gauge is $\int_\Omega p = 0$ via a
scalar Lagrange multiplier; linear solves are direct (MKL PARDISO). Its
credential has four independent legs, all in the verification artifact:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ns-verification
#| output: asis
import json
from pathlib import Path

results_dir = Path("..") / "results"
ver = json.load(open(results_dir / "ns_solver_verification_2026-07-05.json"))
suite = json.load(open(results_dir / "ns_cavity_star_2026-07-05.json"))

conv = ver["mms_square_convergence"]
star = ver["mms_star_resolutions"]["rows"]
star_by_h = {row["target_h"]: row for row in star}
manifest_ver = suite["dataset"]["verification"]

floor_v = max(
    entry.get("label_noise_floor_velocity_max", 0.0)
    for name, entry in manifest_ver.items() if isinstance(entry, dict)
)
floor_p = max(
    entry.get("label_noise_floor_pressure_max", 0.0)
    for name, entry in manifest_ver.items() if isinstance(entry, dict)
)
mom_max = max(
    entry.get("momentum_balance_error_max", 0.0)
    for name, entry in manifest_ver.items() if isinstance(entry, dict)
)
flux_max = max(
    entry.get("boundary_flux_max_abs", 0.0)
    for name, entry in manifest_ver.items() if isinstance(entry, dict)
)
rej = sum(
    entry.get("rejected_attempts_total", 0)
    for name, entry in manifest_ver.items() if isinstance(entry, dict)
)
n_cases = suite["dataset"]["n_cases"]

rows = [
    ("MMS convergence order (unit square)",
     "velocity ~3, pressure ~2",
     f"{conv['velocity_order']:.2f} / {conv['pressure_order']:.2f}"),
    ("MMS velocity rel-L2, star, production $h{=}0.0105$",
     "$\\le 10^{-6}$",
     f"{star_by_h[0.0105]['velocity_rel_l2']:.1e} "
     f"({star_by_h[0.0105]['seconds']:.0f} s/solve)"),
    ("MMS velocity rel-L2, star, first-pass $h{=}0.02$",
     "context (see text)",
     f"{star_by_h[0.02]['velocity_rel_l2']:.1e} "
     f"({star_by_h[0.02]['seconds']:.0f} s/solve)"),
    ("label noise floor, velocity (vs $h/1.5$, worst split)",
     "$\\le 10^{-3}$", f"{floor_v:.1e}"),
    ("label noise floor, pressure (vs $h/1.5$, worst split)",
     "$\\le 10^{-3}$", f"{floor_p:.1e}"),
    ("momentum-balance assembly identity (worst case)",
     "roundoff", f"{mom_max:.1e}"),
    ("discrete boundary flux $|\\oint u_h\\cdot n|$ (worst case)",
     "small, reported", f"{flux_max:.1e}"),
    ("rejected-and-resampled Newton attempts across the catalog",
     "reported", f"{rej} (over {n_cases} cases)"),
]
print("| check | bar | measured |")
print("|---|---|---|")
for name, bar, measured in rows:
    print(f"| {name} | {bar} | {measured} |")
print()
print(": The suite's label credential: manufactured-solutions accuracy "
"and order, the finer-mesh label-noise floor, and the discrete balance "
"certificates, all from checked-in artifacts. {#tbl-ns-verification}")
```

One resolution decision is worth stating plainly, because it was
*revised by a measurement*. The first-pass plan ran production at
$h = 0.02$ — velocity labels two orders under the $10^{-3}$ floor
target, the $10^{-6}$ MMS bar demonstrated separately at $h = 0.01$ —
on the estimate that the $O(h^2)$ pressure floor would land near
$8\times10^{-4}$. The generated catalog measured it at
$2.6$–$3.2\times10^{-3}$ across splits: **the pressure is the binding
field, and the first-pass resolution broke the target.** Generation
had come in far under budget (19.6 minutes for 1,400 cases on 26
workers), so the catalog was regenerated at $h = 0.0105$ (2.7 hours on
20 workers; the finer meshes cost the PARDISO factorizations ~8×) —
where the measured finer-mesh pressure floor comes back under
$10^{-3}$ on four of five splits (worst $8.7\times10^{-4}$ on train;
the unseen-drive split's worst sampled case reads $1.26\times10^{-3}$,
26% over target, reported as-is), the velocity floor sits at
$\le 5.8\times10^{-5}$ everywhere, *and* the MMS velocity bar of
$10^{-6}$ is met at production resolution outright
(@tbl-ns-verification), dissolving the two-resolution compromise. The
Newton robustness grid behind the declared Reynolds band — train
$[10, 200]$, unseen-Re $(200, 300]$ — converges in 4–8 iterations
with occasional backtracking on train-band *and* 0.65-deformation
stars up through Re 400.

#### Arms, and what the nonlinearity does to them {#sec-ns-arms}

catalog, 3 seeds, iteration-17 protocol): the declared-degree flagship
`mt_singpair_q2_pseudo`, the unbounded nonlinear control
`mt_singpair_nl_pseudo`, the pre-registered wall control
`mt_singpair_linear`, the parameter-free `boundary_mean` floor, and the
in-tree Transolver at matched capacity on the same token contract
(coordinates, normals, measures, the rank-1 drive, and $\tilde\nu$ as a
constant channel).
