#### Pre-registered versus measured {#sec-ns-verdicts}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ns-ledger
#| output: asis
import json
from pathlib import Path

suite = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" /
                       "ns_cavity_star_2026-07-05.json"))
v = suite["verdicts"]
p1 = v["P1_linear_wall_grows_with_Re"]
p2 = v["P2_declared_degree_approximation"]
p3 = v["P3_boundary_mean_pressure_floor"]

vel_ratio = p1["velocity_gap_ratio_top_over_bottom"]
prs_ratio = p1["pressure_gap_ratio_top_over_bottom"]
p1_pass = (max(vel_ratio, prs_ratio) >= 3.0)
p1_verdict = "**supported**" if p1_pass else "**not supported**"
p2_verdict = ("degree-2 truncation suffices at these Re"
              if p2["within_2x_seed_sd"]
              else "higher orders matter (q2 trails nl beyond 2x seed sd)")
p3_verdict = "**exact**" if p3["exactly_one"] else "**violated**"

rows = [
    ("P1: linear wall grows with Re "
     "(gap ratio top/bottom Re bin $\\ge 3$, either field)",
     f"velocity {vel_ratio:.1f}x "
     f"(gap {p1['velocity_gap_bottom_bin']:.3f} to "
     f"{p1['velocity_gap_top_bin']:.3f}); "
     f"pressure {prs_ratio:.1f}x "
     f"(gap {p1['pressure_gap_bottom_bin']:.3f} to "
     f"{p1['pressure_gap_top_bin']:.3f})",
     p1_verdict),
    ("P2: declared degree 2 as approximation "
     "(q2 within 2x seed sd of nl on eval_id)",
     f"q2 {p2['q2_eval_id_combined']['mean']:.3f} ± "
     f"{p2['q2_eval_id_combined']['sd']:.3f} vs "
     f"nl {p2['nl_eval_id_combined']['mean']:.3f} ± "
     f"{p2['nl_eval_id_combined']['sd']:.3f}",
     p2_verdict),
    ("P3: boundary-mean pressure floor exactly 1.0",
     f"{p3['boundary_mean_pressure_eval_id']['mean']:.6f}",
     p3_verdict),
]
print("| pre-registered rule | measured | verdict |")
print("|---|---|---|")
for rule, measured, verdict in rows:
    print(f"| {rule} | {measured} | {verdict} |")
print()
print(": The iteration's pre-registered ledger (rules logged in the lab "
"notebook and the driver docstrings before the first training run; "
"numbers from the checked-in artifact). {#tbl-ns-ledger}")
```

**The anomaly, stated plainly.** P1's deciding measurement split: the
pressure leg passed decisively (gap ratio 4.2$\times$, bar 3$\times$),
but the *velocity* leg's low-Re prediction was refuted — the linear
arm's velocity gap to the nonlinear arms is flat at $\approx 0.19$
from Re 10 to Re 300 instead of vanishing toward the Stokes limit.
Two readings, not yet discriminated: (a) Re 10 is simply not Stokes —
at unit drive speed the convective term is already order-one, so the
map's shape-nonlinearity in the drive is present across the whole
sampled band and only the *pressure* (whose convective part is
quadratic-dominant) shows the graded approach; (b) part of the
velocity gap is not the nonlinearity wall at all but a
representation/optimization deficit of the linear read-in on this
feature-rich solver-labeled family. Discriminating (a) from (b) needs
a genuinely Stokes-regime band (Re $\le 1$), which the solver
handles trivially — logged as the follow-up experiment rather than
argued away, and completed as iteration 37 (@sec-ns-lowre). The Transolver baseline's landing point (0.95 combined,
against the floor's 1.19 and the transformer arms' 0.23–0.44) is its
first measurement on a solver-labeled nonlinear suite at the shared
15-epoch protocol; no ordering was pre-registered, and the honest
caveat is that this budget may simply undertrain it — the number is
reported, not weaponized.

**What this iteration establishes, honestly.** The suite exists with a
measured label credential — that is the load-bearing deliverable. The
labels are two orders (velocity) and one order (pressure) below typical
model errors; the pressure floor is the binding one and is stated in
the manifest rather than assumed. The Re-dependent wall gives the
program its first *graded* structural measurement: where the parity
and superposition walls were binary, this one has a height profile
that tracks a physical dimensionless number, and the linear arm's gap
to the nonlinear arms is now a function you can plot rather than a
single 1.0.

**What it does not establish.** At the time of this iteration no
operator-fidelity block (strong-form momentum residual of the model's
own outputs) was emitted by the N-S driver — on the exact-label suites
that block came from autograd against closed-form scales, and porting
it to solver-labeled data was logged as deliberate future work.
Iteration 37 closed that gap (@sec-ns-lowre); the archived runs in
@tbl-ns-arms predate it and keep their em-dash. The suite is
2D, steady, and moderate-Re by construction; nothing here speaks to
turbulence models, and the eval_unseen_Re band (200, 300] stays inside
the solver's verified Newton envelope (grid-verified through Re 400) —
extrapolation beyond the *solver's* comfort zone would make label
quality the confound. Near-wall queries sit at distance 0.02–0.08 with
production meshes graded to $h_b \approx 0.006$ at the boundary; a
higher-Re suite would need boundary-layer-resolving meshes and a fresh
noise-floor measurement.

#### The completed P1 measurable: the Re $\le$ 1 band {#sec-ns-lowre}

The low-Reynolds band settles what the production catalog could not:
the linear read-in class is *not* what costs velocity accuracy in the
near-Stokes regime — a missing parity sector was. The production gap
curve had sat flat at $\approx 0.19$ across Re 10–300, but that band
never reached the Stokes regime the prediction was *about* — at unit
drive speed, Re 10 already has an order-one convective term. Iteration 37
closes this with a **supplementary catalog slice**,
`ns_cavity_star/v1-lowre`: 180 cases with train/eval_id at
$\mathrm{Re}$ log-uniform $[0.5, 5]$ and the unseen-Re band directly
above at $(5, 10]$, generated by the same incremental generator with
the Reynolds band as the *only* moved axis (`--reynolds-range`;
geometry, drive family, $h = 0.0105$, and the full verification
discipline are the production family's, with the measured label-noise
floors in the slice manifest). The linear and nonlinear arms retrain
on the slice at the identical 15-epoch/3-seed protocol, and their
per-case velocity gap joins the archived iteration-36 curve into one
measurement spanning Re 0.5–300. Iteration 38 then closed the one
confound iteration 37 logged inside its own verdict — its linear arm
differed from nl_pseudo in parity machinery and capacity as well as
read-in class — by adding the fair control
`mt_singpair_linear_pseudo` (linear read-in *plus* the nonlinear arm's
`drive_pseudo_dim=8` sector) on both catalogs and recomputing the
whole curve with three arms. Artifacts:
`results/ns_lowre_band_2026-07-05.json`, archive key
`iteration_37_lowre_band`;
`results/ns_linear_pseudo_confound_2026-07-05.json`, archive key
`iteration_38_linear_pseudo_confound`.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ns-lowre-gap
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The completed three-arm gap curve (iterations 37 + 38): each arm's
#|   gap to the nonlinear reference (arm minus nl_pseudo per-case mean
#|   per log-Re bin, eval_id + eval_unseen_Re pooled over 3 seeds)
#|   across Re 0.5-300, velocity left, pressure right. Filled circles:
#|   the v1-lowre slice (108-case train split); open squares: the
#|   production v1 catalog (840-case train split); each side is
#|   internally controlled, so the GAP crosses the seam (dashed) even
#|   though absolute errors do not. The plain linear arm (red)
#|   reproduces iteration 37: velocity gap flat at ~0.13-0.23
#|   everywhere, including the genuinely drive-linear band. The
#|   iteration-38 fair control (blue, the same linear read-in PLUS the
#|   nl arm's drive_pseudo_dim=8 sector) collapses the velocity gap to
#|   zero-or-negative across the entire near-Stokes band and leaves a
#|   graded remainder growing to ~0.10-0.12 by Re 100-213: the
#|   pre-registered REVISION outcome -- iteration 37's flat gap was the
#|   missing parity sector, not the linear read-in class. Both arms'
#|   pressure gaps collapse at low Re and grow to ~0.5: the pressure
#|   wall is physics, and no pseudo sector rescues a drive-linear
#|   read-in from a drive-nonlinear target.
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

confound = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" /
                          "ns_linear_pseudo_confound_2026-07-05.json"))
joined = confound["re_gap_curves"]["joined"]
seam = 10.0
arms = (
    ("mt_singpair_linear", "#e34948", "linear (no pseudo, 106k)"),
    ("mt_singpair_linear_pseudo", "#1a6feb", "linear + pseudo (131k)"),
)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.6, 3.8), sharex=True,
                         sharey=True)
for ax, field in zip(axes, ("velocity", "pressure")):
    low_edge = min(joined[arms[0][0]]["bin_centers"]) / 1.4
    ax.axvspan(low_edge, 1.0, color="#eceaf4", zorder=0)
    ax.axhline(0.0, color="#e1e0d9", lw=1.0, zorder=1)
    ax.axvline(seam, color="#a7a6a1", lw=1.0, ls="--", zorder=1)
    for arm, color, label in arms:
        entry = joined[arm]
        centers = np.array(entry["bin_centers"])
        values = np.array(entry[f"{field}_gap"])
        catalog = np.array(entry["catalog"])
        ax.plot(centers, values, "-", lw=1.3, color=color, label=label,
                zorder=2)
        for cat, marker, face in (("v1-lowre", "o", color),
                                  ("v1", "s", "white")):
            mask = catalog == cat
            ax.plot(centers[mask], values[mask], marker, ms=5, lw=0,
                    color=color, markerfacecolor=face,
                    markeredgecolor=color, zorder=3)
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.set_ylim(-0.12, 0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("case Reynolds number [-]")
    ax.set_title(f"{field} gap to nl_pseudo", fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8, which="both", axis="x")
    for spine in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
axes[0].set_ylabel("arm $-$ nl_pseudo relative $L^2$ gap [-]")
axes[0].text(0.72, -0.108, "near-Stokes\n(drive-linear)",
             fontsize=7.5, color="#52514e", ha="center", va="bottom")
axes[0].text(90.0, -0.108, "convection-dominated",
             fontsize=7.5, color="#52514e", ha="center", va="bottom")
axes[0].annotate("catalog join", (seam, 0.34),
                 xytext=(3, 0), textcoords="offset points",
                 fontsize=7, color="#52514e", rotation=90, va="bottom")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8, frameon=False, loc="upper left")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

**Pre-registered versus measured, completed.** The rule (logged before
the first v1-lowre training run, @sec-nb-iter37): if the velocity map
is near-Stokes-linear at Re $\le 1$, the linear arm's velocity gap
approaches zero at the bottom joined bin (bar: $\le 0.05$ and
$\le 0.25\times$ the top bin) and grows monotonically; falsifier:
bottom-bin gap $\ge 0.1$ (the representation-deficit reading of the
iteration-36 anomaly). Measured: bottom-bin velocity gap **0.184**
against a top-bin 0.204 (ratio 1.10) — **the falsifier fired**. The
velocity leg of P1 is now refuted on a band where the physics cannot
be blamed: at Re $\le 1$ the map is near-Stokes — and the same
figure's pressure gap sitting at zero *proves the linear arm can match
the nonlinear arm on this band when the map is near-linear* — yet the
velocity gap stays at the same $\approx 0.18$ as at Re 300.
Reading (b) of the iteration-36 anomaly survived at that point — but
iteration 37's own verdict flagged the entanglement honestly: its
linear arm lacked the nonlinear arm's pseudo sector and carried
2.2$\times$ fewer parameters, so "linear read-in deficit" was
confounded with "parity/capacity deficit". The
**pressure** leg completes cleanly: its gap is zero within seed noise
across the whole near-Stokes band ($-0.006$, $+0.020$, $-0.042$ at
Re $< 5$ — the linear arm even wins two bins) and climbs to
0.47–0.54 at the top — the graded, physics-tracking wall the
pre-registration predicted, now measured from genuinely-Stokes to
convection-dominated.

**The confound check (iteration 38) — the revision fired.** The fair
control, `mt_singpair_linear_pseudo`: the identical linear field mode
(exact fixed-geometry drive superposition, structurally certified
odd-in-the-drive in-tree) *plus* `drive_pseudo_dim=8` — as matched to
nl_pseudo as the mode allows. Parameters: linear 106,408; linear +
pseudo **131,248**; nl_pseudo 233,108 — the pseudo sector adds 24,840
parameters, and the remaining difference to nl_pseudo *is* the
nonlinear read-in stack, i.e. exactly the treatment variable. Trained
on **both** catalogs (v1-lowre and v1) at the identical
15-epoch/3-seed protocol; pre-registered before the first run, both
outcomes stated in advance: bottom joined-bin velocity gap
$\le 0.05$ REVISES iteration 37 (the deficit was parity/capacity);
$\ge 0.1$ means the read-in-class reading stands, unconfounded.
Measured: bottom-bin velocity gap $\mathbf{-0.024}$ (the linear+pseudo
arm *beats* nl_pseudo on the Stokes band; the plain linear arm's
0.184 reproduces bin-for-bin in the same rerun) — **the revision
fired. Iteration 37's velocity reading is revised: the linear read-in
class is fine where the physics is linear; the flat gap was the
missing pseudo/parity sector, not the read-in.** And with the
confound removed, the velocity gap acquires the graded shape the
original P1 predicted all along: $\approx 0$ (to $-0.05$) across
Re 0.5–7, rising to 0.10–0.12 at Re 100–213 (@fig-ns-lowre-gap, left).
The pressure column sharpens the same story from the other side: the
pseudo sector does *nothing* for the pressure gap (0.016 at the
bottom bin, 0.45–0.54 at the top — bin-for-bin the plain linear
arm's curve), and on the production catalog nl_pseudo still wins
pressure decisively (0.356 vs 0.684 eval_id) — a drive-nonlinear
target stays out of reach of any drive-linear read-in, pseudo sector
or not. That asymmetry, now unconfounded, is the section's finding:
the graded Re-tracking wall is real for *both* fields — velocity's
was just an order of magnitude smaller than the parity artifact that
sat on top of it. One caveat stays on the record: linear+pseudo
matches nl_pseudo's sector structure, not its full width (131k vs
233k); a width-matched linear control was not run, so "capacity" and
"parity machinery" are separated from the read-in class but not from
each other.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ns-lowre
#| output: asis
import json
from pathlib import Path

confound = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" /
                          "ns_linear_pseudo_confound_2026-07-05.json"))
arms = confound["arms_lowre"]
order = ["mt_singpair_nl_pseudo", "mt_singpair_linear_pseudo",
         "mt_singpair_linear"]
labels = {
    "mt_singpair_nl_pseudo": "MT nonlinear + pseudo",
    "mt_singpair_linear_pseudo": "MT linear + pseudo (iter-38 control)",
    "mt_singpair_linear": "MT linear (wall control)",
}
splits = ["eval_id", "eval_unseen_Re", "eval_unseen_geometry",
          "eval_unseen_drive_profile"]
headers = (["arm", "params"] + [s.replace("eval_", "").replace("_", "-")
                                for s in splits]
           + ["momentum res. (ID)", "divergence res. (ID)"])
print("| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |")
print("|" + "---|" * len(headers))
for arm in order:
    row = [labels[arm], f"{arms[arm]['parameters']:,}"]
    for split in splits:
        cell = arms[arm]["splits"][split]["combined"]
        row.append(f"{cell['mean']:.3f} ± {cell['sd']:.3f}")
    for key in ("momentum_residual", "divergence_residual"):
        cell = arms[arm]["fidelity"][key]["eval_id"]
        row.append(f"{cell['mean']:.2f} ± {cell['sd']:.2f}")
    print("| " + " | ".join(row) + " |")
print()
n_train = confound["dataset"]["lowre_split_sizes"]["train"]
print(": The v1-lowre slice arms (combined relative $L^2$, mean ± sd "
f"over 3 seeds, {n_train}-case train split; iteration-37 arms plus "
"the iteration-38 confound control) with the suite's first populated "
"fidelity columns: the strong-form momentum residual "
"$\\|\\tilde\\nu\\Delta u - (u\\cdot\\nabla)u - \\nabla p\\| / "
"\\|(u\\cdot\\nabla)u\\|$ of the model's own prediction and the "
"matching divergence norm (float64 autograd, 32 interior queries, "
"2 cases/split; $\\tilde\\nu$ from the case -- the model never sees "
"the PDE, the metric does). {#tbl-ns-lowre}")
```

The fidelity block itself is the iteration's second deliverable — the
N-S port of the @sec-fidelity-columns convention to solver-labeled
data, where no closed-form scale exists: the residual is normalized by
the prediction's *own* advection norm, and the instrument is certified
in-tree before use — the exact Kovasznay solution scores $\sim 0$
*only* when the metric uses the case's $\tilde\nu$ (pinning the
"$\tilde\nu$ from the case" plumbing), and a rigid rotation with its
pressure dropped scores exactly 1
(`test_fidelity_residuals_certify_the_instrument`). As on every suite
since the column became first-class, the strong-form numbers are
diagnostics of *how* the arms fit, not who wins: they complement the
$L^2$ columns and cannot be gamed by a constant field, which zeroes
the interior strong form while failing the boundary conditions — the
note in the driver states this explicitly. Read the low-Re magnitudes
with the normalization in mind: near Stokes the true advection is
small while $\tilde\nu$ is order one, so the advection-normalized
residual amplifies second-derivative model error by
$\sim \tilde\nu/\|(u\cdot\nabla)u\|$ — the O(10) values in
@tbl-ns-lowre say the predictions' derivatives do not satisfy the
operator (consistent with every suite since @sec-fidelity-columns:
$L^2$-fit fields, unsatisfied operators). The three-arm ordering
tracks the velocity story exactly: the plain linear arm's momentum
residual (47.7) and divergence norm (2.70) sit 2–3$\times$ above the
other two, while the iteration-38 linear+pseudo control lands beside
nl_pseudo (momentum 22.2 vs 16.1) and *beats* it on divergence (0.85
vs 1.07) — the fidelity instrument independently confirms that the
pseudo sector, not the nonlinear read-in, is what the plain linear
arm's velocity was missing.
